The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8a4c10;">Gene A</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #8a4c10;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8a4c10;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c68;">Gene K</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006c68;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c68;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #843994;">Gene T</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #843994;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #695f17;">Gene C</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #695f17;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #695f17;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #305f99;">Gene D</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #305f99;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #305f99;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #953270;">Gene K</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #953270;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #953270;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a12d45;">Gene A</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #a12d45;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a12d45;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006f51;">Gene J</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006f51;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006f51;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #305f99;">Gene P</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #305f99;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #305f99;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8a4c10;">Gene E</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #8a4c10;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8a4c10;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006f51;">Gene X</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006f51;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006f51;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6c3fb7;">Gene Y</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #6c3fb7;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6c3fb7;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #695f17;">Gene A</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #695f17;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #695f17;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a79;">Gene C</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006a79;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a79;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #953270;">Gene Y</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #953270;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #953270;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a12d45;">Gene C</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #a12d45;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a12d45;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #526711;">Gene E</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #526711;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #526711;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #236586;">Gene X</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #236586;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #236586;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8a4c10;">Gene D</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #8a4c10;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8a4c10;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c68;">Gene E</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006c68;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c68;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4752b5;">Gene H</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #4752b5;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4752b5;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7c5603;">Gene A</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #7c5603;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7c5603;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c68;">Gene C</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006c68;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c68;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6c3fb7;">Gene H</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #6c3fb7;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6c3fb7;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9c391c;">Gene F</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #9c391c;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9c391c;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006f51;">Gene H</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006f51;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006f51;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6c3fb7;">Gene Y</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #6c3fb7;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6c3fb7;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #695f17;">Gene N</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #695f17;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #695f17;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a79;">Gene W</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006a79;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a79;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #953270;">Gene Y</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #953270;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #953270;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8a4c10;">Gene B</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #8a4c10;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8a4c10;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1c7029;">Gene C</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #1c7029;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1c7029;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #305f99;">Gene D</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #305f99;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #305f99;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #695f17;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #236586;">Gene P</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #236586;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #236586;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #953270;">Gene T</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #953270;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #953270;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8a4c10;">Gene A</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #8a4c10;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8a4c10;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c68;">Gene T</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006c68;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c68;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4752b5;">Gene X</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #4752b5;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4752b5;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8a4c10;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c68;">Gene K</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006c68;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c68;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #843994;">Gene M</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #843994;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #843994;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7c5603;">Gene D</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #7c5603;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7c5603;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006f51;">Gene J</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006f51;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006f51;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #843994;">Gene R</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #843994;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #843994;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8a4c10;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1c7029;">Gene B</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #1c7029;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1c7029;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #236586;">Gene Y</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #236586;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #236586;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8a4c10;">Gene B</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #8a4c10;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8a4c10;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006f51;">Gene T</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006f51;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006f51;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6c3fb7;">Gene Y</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #6c3fb7;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6c3fb7;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7c5603;">Gene D</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #7c5603;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7c5603;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #305f99;">Gene R</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #305f99;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #305f99;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #953270;">Gene W</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #953270;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #953270;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #695f17;">Gene M</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #695f17;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #695f17;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a79;">Gene W</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006a79;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a79;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6c3fb7;">Gene X</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #6c3fb7;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6c3fb7;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a12d45;">Gene C</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #a12d45;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a12d45;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #526711;">Gene W</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #526711;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #526711;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a79;">Gene X</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006a79;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a79;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8a4c10;">Gene C</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #8a4c10;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8a4c10;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a79;">Gene J</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006a79;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a79;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #843994;">Gene X</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #843994;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #843994;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8a4c10;">Gene F</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #8a4c10;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8a4c10;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1c7029;">Gene J</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #1c7029;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1c7029;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6c3fb7;">Gene N</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #6c3fb7;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #695f17;">Gene D</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #695f17;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #695f17;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c68;">Gene F</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006c68;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c68;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #953270;">Gene W</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #953270;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #953270;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a12d45;">Gene M</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #a12d45;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a12d45;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1c7029;">Gene R</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #1c7029;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1c7029;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #305f99;">Gene T</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #305f99;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #305f99;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7c5603;">Gene D</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #7c5603;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7c5603;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006f51;">Gene F</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006f51;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006f51;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #953270;">Gene H</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #953270;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #953270;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a12d45;">Gene D</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #a12d45;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a12d45;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1c7029;">Gene M</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #1c7029;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1c7029;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4752b5;">Gene Y</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #4752b5;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4752b5;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7c5603;">Gene A</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #7c5603;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7c5603;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006f51;">Gene N</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006f51;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006f51;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #843994;">Gene W</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #843994;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #843994;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7c5603;">Gene A</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #7c5603;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7c5603;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006f51;">Gene T</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006f51;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006f51;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #953270;">Gene X</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #953270;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #953270;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8a4c10;">Gene D</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #8a4c10;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8a4c10;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006f51;">Gene R</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006f51;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006f51;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #843994;">Gene X</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #843994;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #843994;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8a4c10;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c68;">Gene F</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006c68;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c68;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #843994;">Gene X</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #843994;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #843994;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7c5603;">Gene A</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #7c5603;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7c5603;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006f51;">Gene M</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006f51;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006f51;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #843994;">Gene R</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #843994;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #843994;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8a4c10;">Gene K</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #8a4c10;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8a4c10;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006f51;">Gene M</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006f51;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006f51;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #305f99;">Gene P</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #305f99;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #305f99;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8a4c10;">Gene J</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #8a4c10;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8a4c10;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006f51;">Gene N</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006f51;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006f51;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4752b5;">Gene P</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #4752b5;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4752b5;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7c5603;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006f51;">Gene M</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006f51;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006f51;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #953270;">Gene N</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #953270;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8a4c10;">Gene B</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #8a4c10;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8a4c10;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1c7029;">Gene H</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #1c7029;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1c7029;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #236586;">Gene P</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #236586;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #236586;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #526711;">Gene E</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #526711;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #526711;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a79;">Gene P</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006a79;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a79;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6c3fb7;">Gene W</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #6c3fb7;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6c3fb7;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8a4c10;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006f51;">Gene E</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006f51;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006f51;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6c3fb7;">Gene P</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #6c3fb7;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7c5603;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #236586;">Gene K</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #236586;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #236586;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #843994;">Gene W</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #843994;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype.
